answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on reputation or claim shared rewards. The protocol caps each stake’s influence and slashes it when independent audits prove coordinated fraud, so splitting one bankroll across a thousand aliases yields no extra weight. A raven may spot a garden of lotus accounts, but the defense is the attacker’s cost: capital tied up in each identity, plus losses when caught.
